title: Equivariant mates and their rational/common-stage coefficient transport
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories with endofunctors $P_{\mathcal A},P_{\mathcal B},P_{\mathcal C},P_{\mathcal D}$. Use their fixed-pair categories [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], whose objects are $(K,\theta:P K\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$ and arrows obey $u\theta_K=\theta_LP(u)$. Let $L_1:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B\dashv R_1$, $L_2:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D\dashv R_2$ be adjunctions, with units $\eta_i$ and counits $\varepsilon_i$, and let $U:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$, $V:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$ be functors. Suppose all six functors have specified lifts to these fixed-pair categories, with the specified units and counits lifting the carrier units and counits. Let $\alpha:L_2U\to VL_1$ be a natural transformation inducing morphisms of fixed pairs. Its right mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]
$$\alpha^\flat_d=R_2V(\varepsilon_{1,d})\,R_2(\alpha_{R_1d})\,\eta_{2,UR_1d}:UR_1d\to R_2Vd$$
induces a natural transformation between the lifted functors. Pasting on the non-adjoint sides, composition of the adjunctions, and change of adjunction by a transformation give exactly the mates specified by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1)--(3), as equalities of fixed-pair morphisms. The carrier of the lifted mate is the specified three-factor mate, not a choice of a naturally isomorphic map.

For coefficient transport, fix $p\ne\ell$, $q=p^a$ with $a\geq1$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite in a fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Take the categories above to be the stipulated constructible coefficient categories on their geometric fibers, the endofunctors to be geometric Frobenius pullback, and fixed pairs to be [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Use the rationalization and common-stage operation and map constructions of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-exchange-projection]. Assume that the comparisons for the functors involved intertwine the units, counits and $\alpha$, are identities for identity extensions, and satisfy the tower cocycle. The rational image of an integral mate equals the mate of the rational images. Under a finite field extension, the transported mate equals the mate of the transported maps, conjugated by the supplied comparisons at its source and target. These identities also hold for pasted mates. Their common-stage classes are independent of the finite coefficient field and of the morphism representative. They apply to every morphism of the localized/common-stage categories and every Weil structure there, without requiring a Frobenius-stable integral lattice. Finally, if a lifted mate or comparison has an invertible carrier on the stipulated domain, its carrier inverse is a morphism of fixed pairs, hence it is an isomorphism there. Equivariance alone makes no additional comparison invertible.

proof.text: For coefficient transport, cancel the source comparison and expand the mate. Naturality moves the right-adjoint comparison past the square and the counit; naturality of the vertical comparison and compatibility of the first counit identify the final factors. Apply the square compatibility after mapping by the second right adjoint. The second unit compatibility cancels the first factors. Finally, naturality of the target unit and square gives the target mate. This is valid for arbitrary categories and functors; specialize it to the actual rationalization, finite-stage transition, and common-stage inclusion functors. The exact rational formula is simply map_comp on the three mate factors.

proof.text: Functoriality and associativity prove transport of a threefold composite: the two intermediate comparison/inverse pairs cancel. For composite comparisons, expand their definition. The identity follows by mapping the identity equation for the first operation through the second and then using its identity equation. For the tower, naturality of the second operation comparison interchanges the middle factors. Combine the three maps under the second operation, apply the first tower equation, and then the second tower equation.

proof.text: Naturality for every common-stage arrow is naturality of the mate transformation itself. For representatives, use GeneralAlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.representatives to turn equality at a common later stage into equality of the two quotient arrows; substitute and apply naturality. For rational and common-stage Weil objects, apply fixedPair_mate to the actual Frobenius endofunctors, and append naturality of the lifted mate. No integral lattice or integral representative of a rational inverse is required.
